scope: Operation GALVANIC Branch-B contact chain from late 1943-11-22 through the first firm Japanese external sensor contact on the morning of 1943-11-23. Stops before weapon release.
adjudication_rule: Use EM warning -> bearing history/battle preparation -> sensor contact -> track -> weapon-quality. This ledger closes through SENSOR CONTACT / partial operational TRACK only; no strike or surface-weapon result is inherited from the old settlement.

environment.weather_center: Partly cloudy / broken tropical trade-weather regime; working visibility 10-20 nmi in clear sectors, easterly 10-18 kt, slight-to-moderate sea. Historical GALVANIC aerology reports 12-20 mile visibility and satisfactory reconnaissance/landing weather through succeeding days; Branch D-day is shifted, so this is a fallback band rather than an exact copied observation.
environment.moon: Waning crescent. Roughly 15-20% illuminated on 11/23 and about 10% on 11/24; moon is mainly a pre-dawn object, leaving the evening/first half of night very dark.
environment.operational_effect: Daybreak visual search is workable; the following night strongly favors concealment and makes recontact/reporting more important than moonlit visual acquisition.

search_system.southern_marshalls_priority_sector: Mili-Jaluit-Taroa/Kwajalein correlation line, with visual/RI-DF/passive ESM and selected warning-radar inputs. Do not assume every island has every Branch device.

passive_ESM_fit.centered_geometry: At least two reporting nodes across the southern-Marshalls approach sector have metric-band passive warning/DF integration by 1943H2; exact box serials are not asserted.
passive_ESM_fit.capability: Bearing/warning against compatible US metric emissions; no range, no reliable ship type, no SG/10-cm immunity.
passive_ESM_fit.sensitivity: One effective node delays/narrows the warning less efficiently; three nodes improve bearing history. The centered first-contact conclusion does not require fleetwide ESM.

air_search_assets_relevant_to_contact.legacy_long_range: H8K/H6K/G4M-recon class and mature E13A/F1M search/observation assets remain the broad-search backbone; exact local type counts are still being closed for weapon-release adjudication.
air_search_assets_relevant_to_contact.D4Y: Use for fast confirmation when locally assigned; not assumed everywhere.
air_search_assets_relevant_to_contact.Zuiun: Small first-detachment layer is allowed in the Marshall-side network by 11/23. It is held primarily for re-search/fast confirmation, not credited with creating the initial broad-ocean detection by itself.
air_search_assets_relevant_to_contact.working_dawn_search_effort: About 7-10 useful long-range/floatplane search sorties across the southern search ring is the centered event-level effort after fatigue, maintenance and other duties; 1-2 fast re-search/confirmation sorties can be generated if the local Zuiun/D4Y allocation is serviceable.
air_search_assets_relevant_to_contact.anti_error: Do not add national aircraft inventories or the entire 4-7-ready Zuiun working regional band to one base.

US_emission_and_route_state.route: Branch routing is not historical one-for-one because Midway is Japanese-held and Espiritu Santo/New Caledonia are unavailable. However, by D-1 carrier cover and assault forces must enter the Gilbert/southern-Marshall operating geometry to suppress Mili/Jaluit/Tarawa/Makin and cover the landings.
US_emission_and_route_state.emission_state: Fast-carrier/CVL formations cannot remain completely radio/radar silent while running CAP, search, ASW, launch/recovery and fighter direction in a known Japanese air-threat area. Some compatible metric emissions are therefore available to passive warning even under disciplined EMCON.
US_emission_and_route_state.screen_effect: US radar/CAP makes Japanese scouts vulnerable and can break continuous shadowing; it does not prevent a scout from transmitting a short contact report before interception.

contact_sequence.result: Intermittent compatible emissions plus RI/DF/traffic and the already-tight Gilbert-Marshall target inference produce a probable large US naval-force bearing sector. No carrier identity or range is obtained.

Repeated/shifted bearings and external indicators narrow the priority dawn-search sectors. Search crews, selected attack units, submarine sectors and light-surface readiness are raised. This buys preparation time but is still not a target solution.

Dawn search launches into the narrowed southern/eastern approach sectors. Legacy long-range aircraft carry the wide arcs; faster scarce aircraft are reserved or redirected for suspicious-contact confirmation.

A Japanese long-range scout visually acquires one US carrier-cover formation in the Gilbert-southern-Marshall operating area and transmits before CAP can fully erase the report. The centered report supports 'carrier task group / multiple flight decks probable, heavy escorts present' but not an exact named OOB.
contact_sequence.contact_target: One fast-carrier/CVL cover formation, not the entire US fast-carrier pool and not yet the complete assault convoy disposition.

contact_sequence.result: A re-search/confirmation attempt, aided where available by D4Y/Zuiun-speed and the narrowed sector, refreshes the contact enough to validate continued carrier activity. US CAP/radar pressure prevents a clean continuous shadow. Report latency/position error remains combat-relevant.
contact_sequence.working_report_age: roughly 20-50 minutes at the receiving operational command after confirmation
contact_sequence.working_position_error: roughly 20-40 nmi class after relay and target movement; course/speed only approximate

centered_outcome.first_firm_external_contact: Morning 1943-11-23, centered about 06:30 local, by Japanese air reconnaissance after earlier passive/DF cueing.
what_Japan_knows: A major US carrier-covered operation is immediately present in the Gilbert-southern-Marshall battle space.
At least one carrier task group is visually confirmed and large enough to justify immediate strike planning.
The prior amphibious inference is strongly reinforced.
what_Japan_does_not_know: The exact disposition of all US CV/CVL groups.
The exact assault convoy location and screen geometry.
Whether the sighted carrier group is the best target or a covering/interceptor element.
A weapon-quality range/course solution valid hours later.
centered_outcome.US_awareness: US radar/CAP likely detects or chases at least one scout/confirming aircraft, so US commanders know Japanese reconnaissance is active; they do not necessarily know how much of the report was transmitted or correlated with passive bearings.

historical_fallback_comparison.note: Historical GALVANIC also produced a D-1 Japanese carrier-force sighting; this is used as a detectability sanity check, not copied as an exact Branch position/time. Branch B has healthier Marshall air and better cue-to-confirm process, but different US routing and D-day.
historical_fallback_comparison.historical_sanity_check: A Japanese account summarized by Stan Jersey places discovery of two US carrier striking groups at about 0630 on historical D-1 (19 Nov), about 100 miles south/southwest of Tarawa.

qualitative_threshold_test.reason: The old detailed settlement did not explicitly carry a firm D-1 cue-to-contact chain and placed its first major Marshall night air strike after the Branch landings. The re-audit now yields a credible firm carrier contact early on 11/23, while the local air wallet is healthier and the following night is very dark. This creates a real pre-D-day 11/23-24 strike/recontact decision gate and must be resolved before returning to the old sequence.
qualitative_threshold_test.not_yet_changed: US landing success, named carrier damage and the four-carrier Japanese main-body decision are not changed yet. The threshold is an operational branch gate, not a pre-awarded hit.

next_boundary.question: Can Japan maintain/reacquire a sufficiently fresh target track to launch a night land-air strike and/or light-surface one-pass probe before D-day, and what does US radar/CAP/screen geometry do to that attempt?
must_close_before_weapon_release: base-by-base Marshall/Gilbert attack/recon ready aircraft and night-qualified crews
named light-surface group hulls/readiness/fuel and launch position
submarine on-station hulls/patrol-days and approach sectors
US fast-carrier/assault-force screen and route geometry on 11/23
actual emitting/radar-equipped US formations and Japanese selected ESM-equipped nodes/ships
event weather/cloud/visibility and recovery-base condition after D-1 suppression

sources: NHHC, Occupation of the Gilbert Islands / aerology report (historical weather fallback)
NHHC, H-025-1 Operation Galvanic (carrier/CVE and Japanese counterattack context)
Radar and the Fighter Directors, Gilbert and Marshall Islands chapter (US radar/CAP/fighter-direction context)
Stan Jersey, Japanese Forces in the Gilbert and Nauru Islands (historical D-1 Japanese sighting sanity check)
